summary: Grackle models the outcome of every fallible operation (parsing, compilation, elaboration, query interpretation, validation, effects) as `Result[A]` — an `Ior`-like ADT with four cases: `Success` (value only), `Warning` (value + a non-empty chain of `Problem`s), `Failure` (problems only, no value), and `InternalError` (a `Throwable` representing a bug/unexpected condition, not a user-facing GraphQL error). `Problem` is the GraphQL-spec-shaped error object (message, locations, path, extensions) that gets serialised into the `errors` array of a response. The companion provides constructors and conversions, while `ResultInstances` supplies cats typeclass instances (`MonadError`, `Traverse`, `Parallel`, `Semigroup`, `Eq`) so results compose with `for`/`traverse`/`parMapN` and accumulate problems. At the response boundary `Mapping.mkResponse` folds a `Result[Json]` into a GraphQL response: `Success`→`{data}`, `Warning`→`{errors,data}`, `Failure`→`{errors}` (no data), and `InternalError`→raised into the effect `F`. `ValidationFailure` is a separate, schema/mapping-construction-time diagnostic type (with `Severity`) used for richly-formatted, colourised validation messages, distinct from runtime `Problem`s.

keyConcepts.name: Four-case Result ADT (Ior semantics)
keyConcepts.explanation: Result[+T] is sealed with Success(value), Warning(problems, value), Failure(problems) and InternalError(error). It generalises Either/Ior: Warning carries BOTH a value and accumulated problems (like Ior.Both), Failure carries only problems, and InternalError is a fourth case for Throwables that escape the normal problem channel. hasValue is true for Success/Warning; hasProblems is true for Warning/Failure; isInternalError isolates the bug case.

keyConcepts.name: Problem vs InternalError vs ValidationFailure
keyConcepts.explanation: Problem is a user-facing GraphQL error (serialised into the errors array). InternalError wraps a Throwable that should surface as an effect-level failure (M.raiseError in mkResponse), NOT as a GraphQL error — it represents an internal bug/unexpected state. ValidationFailure (with Severity Error/Warning/Info) is a third, unrelated diagnostic used only when building/validating a Schema or Mapping; ValidationException wraps a NonEmptyList of them.

keyConcepts.name: Problem accumulation via Semigroup/Applicative
keyConcepts.explanation: Problems accumulate as a NonEmptyChain[Problem]. flatMap and the MonadError carry warnings forward and merge problem chains; the Parallel/Applicative ap and the Semigroup combine accumulate problems from both sides (Failure ++ Failure = Failure with both, but a short-circuit on InternalError). This is how multiple validation/compilation errors are reported at once rather than failing on the first.

keyConcepts.name: Result combinators & syntax
keyConcepts.explanation: Instance methods: map, flatMap, traverse, fold, foldLeft/Right, toEither, toOption, withProblems, combine, getOrElse, plus predicates hasValue/isFailure/hasProblems/isInternalError/toProblems. Companion constructors: apply/pure/success, warning, failure, internalError, fromOption, fromEither, fromProblems, catchNonFatal, combineAllWithDefault. Extension syntax in grackle.syntax: a.success, opt.toResult(ifNone), opt.toResultOrError(ifNone).

keyConcepts.name: ResultT monad transformer
keyConcepts.explanation: ResultT[F[_], A](value: F[Result[A]]) lifts Result into an effect F (typically a cats-effect IO or fs2 Stream). It is used pervasively in the interpreter/mapping to thread Result through F with for-comprehensions; it preserves Warning/Failure/InternalError propagation and problem accumulation across the F boundary. Constructors: liftF, pure, fromResult, success, warning, failure, internalError.

keyConcepts.name: Mapping failures to the GraphQL response
keyConcepts.explanation: Mapping.mkResponse(result: Result[Json]): F[Json] is the single boundary that turns a Result into a spec response. Success→{"data":..}; Warning→{"errors":[..],"data":..} (errors AND data present); Failure→{"errors":[..]} (no data key); InternalError→M.raiseError(throwable). The overload mkResponse(data, errors) also emits a synthetic {"errors":[{"message":"Invalid query"}]} when both data and errors are empty.

keyConcepts.name: Severity ordering for validation
keyConcepts.explanation: ValidationFailure.Severity is a sealed trait (Error > Warning > Info) with a cats Order instance (Error=3, Warning=2, Info=1), letting validators filter/threshold diagnostics by severity (e.g. only fail on Error, surface Warning/Info).

keyTypes.name: Result[+T]
keyTypes.signature: sealed trait Result[+T]
keyTypes.purpose: The core fallible-outcome type; Ior-like ADT over a value of type T and/or accumulated Problems, plus an InternalError case for Throwables.

keyTypes.name: Result.Success
keyTypes.signature: final case class Success[+T](value: T) extends Result[T]
keyTypes.purpose: A successful result carrying only a value (no problems).

keyTypes.name: Result.Warning
keyTypes.signature: final case class Warning[+T](problems: NonEmptyChain[Problem], value: T) extends Result[T]
keyTypes.purpose: A result carrying BOTH a value and a non-empty chain of problems; surfaces as data + errors in the response.

keyTypes.name: Result.Failure
keyTypes.signature: final case class Failure(problems: NonEmptyChain[Problem]) extends Result[Nothing]
keyTypes.purpose: A failed result carrying only problems and no value; surfaces as errors-only response.

keyTypes.name: Result.InternalError
keyTypes.signature: final case class InternalError(error: Throwable) extends Result[Nothing]
keyTypes.purpose: An internal/unexpected error wrapping a Throwable; raised into the effect F rather than reported as a GraphQL error.

keyTypes.name: Result.fold
keyTypes.signature: def fold[U](failure: NonEmptyChain[Problem] => U, success: T => U, warning: (NonEmptyChain[Problem], T) => U, error: Throwable => U): U
keyTypes.purpose: Exhaustive eliminator handling all four cases.

keyTypes.name: Result.flatMap
keyTypes.signature: def flatMap[U](f: T => Result[U]): Result[U]
keyTypes.purpose: Monadic bind; merges/propagates warning problem chains and short-circuits on Failure/InternalError.

keyTypes.name: Result.withProblems
keyTypes.signature: def withProblems(problems: NonEmptyChain[Problem]): Result[T]
keyTypes.purpose: Attach extra problems: Success becomes Warning, Warning/Failure accumulate, InternalError is unchanged.

keyTypes.name: Result.combine
keyTypes.signature: def combine[U >: T](that: Result[U])(implicit S: Semigroup[U]): Result[U]
keyTypes.purpose: Semigroup combine that merges values via S and accumulates problems across both sides (downgrading Failure to Warning when the other side has a value).

keyTypes.name: Result.toProblems
keyTypes.signature: def toProblems: Chain[Problem]
keyTypes.purpose: Extract accumulated problems as a Chain (empty for Success/InternalError); used by mkResponse to build the errors array.

keyTypes.name: Result.toEither
keyTypes.signature: def toEither: Either[Either[Throwable, NonEmptyChain[Problem]], T]
keyTypes.purpose: Convert to a nested Either where the left distinguishes InternalError (inner Left) from Failure (inner Right).

keyTypes.name: Result.failure
keyTypes.signature: def failure[A](s: String): Result[A]   /   def failure[A](p: Problem): Result[A]
keyTypes.purpose: Construct a Failure from a message string or an explicit Problem.

keyTypes.name: Result.warning
keyTypes.signature: def warning[A](warning: Problem, value: A): Result[A]   /   def warning[A](warning: String, value: A): Result[A]
keyTypes.purpose: Construct a Warning from a single problem/message plus a value.

keyTypes.name: Result.internalError
keyTypes.signature: def internalError[A](err: Throwable): Result[A]   /   def internalError[A](err: String): Result[A]
keyTypes.purpose: Construct an InternalError from a Throwable, or wrap a String in a new Throwable.

keyTypes.name: Result.fromOption
keyTypes.signature: def fromOption[A](oa: Option[A], ifNone: => Problem): Result[A]
keyTypes.purpose: Lift an Option, producing a Failure (ifNone) when empty. There is a String overload guarded by a DummyImplicit.

keyTypes.name: Result.fromEither
keyTypes.signature: def fromEither[A](ea: Either[Problem, A]): Result[A]
keyTypes.purpose: Lift an Either, mapping Left to Failure. A String-left overload exists (DummyImplicit-guarded).

keyTypes.name: Result.fromProblems
keyTypes.signature: def fromProblems(problems: Seq[Problem]): Result[Unit]   /   def fromProblems(problems: Chain[Problem]): Result[Unit]
keyTypes.purpose: Yield Result.unit when there are no problems, otherwise a Failure; used to fold validation problem lists into a Result.

keyTypes.name: Result.catchNonFatal
keyTypes.signature: def catchNonFatal[T](body: => T): Result[T]
keyTypes.purpose: Run a thunk, returning Success or, on a NonFatal throwable, InternalError.

keyTypes.name: Result.combineAllWithDefault
keyTypes.signature: def combineAllWithDefault[T](ress: List[Result[T]], default: => T): Result[List[T]]
keyTypes.purpose: Combine a list of results preserving order/length by substituting a default for failed elements, accumulating all problems; returns the first InternalError if any.

keyTypes.name: grackleMonadErrorForResult
keyTypes.signature: implicit val grackleMonadErrorForResult: MonadError[Result, Either[Throwable, NonEmptyChain[Problem]]]
keyTypes.purpose: cats MonadError instance; the error type Either[Throwable, NEC[Problem]] unifies InternalError (left) and Failure (right) for raiseError/handleErrorWith.

keyTypes.name: grackleParallelForResult
keyTypes.signature: implicit def grackleParallelForResult[E]: Parallel.Aux[Result, Result]
keyTypes.purpose: Parallel instance whose Applicative ap accumulates problems from both operands (enables parMapN error accumulation).

keyTypes.name: grackleSemigroupForResult / grackleEqForResult / grackleTraverseFunctorForResult
keyTypes.signature: implicit def grackleSemigroupForResult[A: Semigroup]: Semigroup[Result[A]]; implicit def grackleEqForResult[A: Eq]: Eq[Result[A]]; implicit val grackleTraverseFunctorForResult: Traverse[Result]
keyTypes.purpose: Semigroup (via combine), Eq (via ===), and Traverse instances for Result.

keyTypes.name: ResultT[F[_], A]
keyTypes.signature: final case class ResultT[F[_], A](value: F[Result[A]])
keyTypes.purpose: Monad transformer stacking Result inside an effect F; map/flatMap preserve problem accumulation. Companion provides liftF/pure/fromResult/success/warning/failure/internalError.

keyTypes.name: Problem
keyTypes.signature: final case class Problem(message: String, locations: List[(Int, Int)] = Nil, path: List[String] = Nil, extensions: Option[JsonObject] = None)
keyTypes.purpose: GraphQL-spec error object. Has a human-readable toString and a circe Encoder producing the response error JSON; Eq ignores extensions.

keyTypes.name: Problem.ProblemEncoder
keyTypes.signature: implicit val ProblemEncoder: Encoder[Problem]
keyTypes.purpose: circe encoder: emits message always, and locations/path/extensions only when non-empty; locations become {line,col} objects.

keyTypes.name: Mapping.mkResponse (Result overload)
keyTypes.signature: def mkResponse(result: Result[Json]): F[Json]
keyTypes.purpose: Boundary that turns a Result[Json] into a GraphQL response: InternalError → M.raiseError; otherwise mkResponse(result.toOption, result.toProblems).

keyTypes.name: Mapping.mkResponse (data/errors overload)
keyTypes.signature: def mkResponse(data: Option[Json], errors: Chain[Problem]): Json
keyTypes.purpose: Assemble the JSON: emits data and/or errors; when both empty emits a synthetic errors array {"message":"Invalid query"}.

keyTypes.name: ValidationFailure
keyTypes.signature: abstract class ValidationFailure(val severity: Severity) extends AnsiColor
keyTypes.purpose: Schema/mapping-construction diagnostic with a coloured, padded formattedMessage and toErrorMessage; distinct from runtime Problem.

keyTypes.name: ValidationFailure.Severity
keyTypes.signature: sealed trait Severity extends Product  (Error, Warning, Info) with implicit Order[Severity]
keyTypes.purpose: Diagnostic severity with a total ordering (Error=3 > Warning=2 > Info=1).

keyTypes.name: ValidationException
keyTypes.signature: final case class ValidationException(failures: NonEmptyList[ValidationFailure]) extends RuntimeException with NoStackTrace
keyTypes.purpose: Throwable aggregating validation failures; its getMessage concatenates each failure's toErrorMessage.

keyTypes.name: syntax.ResultIdOps / ResultOptionOps
keyTypes.signature: implicit class ResultIdOps[A](val a: A) { def success: Result[A] }; implicit class ResultOptionOps[T](val opt: Option[T]) { def toResult(ifNone: => Problem); def toResult(ifNone: => String); def toResultOrError(ifNone: => Throwable); def toResultOrError(ifNone: => String) }
keyTypes.purpose: Ergonomic extension syntax (import grackle.syntax._) for lifting values/options into Result.

minimalExamples.title: Constructing the four Result cases
minimalExamples.code:
import cats.data.NonEmptyChain
import grackle.{Problem, Result}

val ok:    Result[Int] = Result.Success(42)
val ok2:   Result[Int] = Result(42)          // == Result.success(42) == Result.pure(42)
val warn:  Result[Int] = Result.warning("deprecated field used", 42) // Warning(problems, 42)
val fail:  Result[Int] = Result.failure("No field 'foo' for type Character")
val failP: Result[Int] = Result.failure(Problem("boom", path = List("user", "name")))
val boom:  Result[Int] = Result.internalError(new RuntimeException("bug"))

assert(ok.toOption == Some(42))
assert(warn.hasValue && warn.hasProblems)
assert(fail.isFailure && fail.toOption.isEmpty)
assert(boom.isInternalError)
minimalExamples.explanation: Shows every constructor on the Result companion and the predicates that distinguish the cases. Mirrors the Arbitrary generator in ResultSuite.scala (lines 42-54) and the failure assertions in CompilerSuite.scala.

minimalExamples.title: Problem JSON encoding (the errors array shape)
minimalExamples.explanation: Verbatim from ProblemSuite.scala (encoding/toString tests). Empty locations/path/extensions are dropped from the JSON; a single-line location (a==b) renders as the bare number rather than a range.

minimalExamples.title: Result composes in a for-comprehension and accumulates warnings
minimalExamples.code:
import grackle.Result
import grackle.syntax._   // for `.success`, `.toResult`

val r: Result[Int] =
  for {
    a <- Result.warning("w1", 1)   // Warning(w1, 1)
    b <- 2.success                 // Success(2)
    c <- Option(3).toResult("missing c")
  } yield a + b + c

// r == Result.Warning(NonEmptyChain(Problem("w1")), 6)
assert(r.toOption == Some(6))
assert(r.toProblems.toList.map(_.message) == List("w1"))
minimalExamples.explanation: flatMap carries the Warning's problem chain forward while keeping the value; a Failure anywhere in the chain would short-circuit to Failure. Uses the grackle.syntax extension methods (.success, Option#toResult).

minimalExamples.title: A field-level warning surfaces as BOTH data and errors
minimalExamples.explanation: Verbatim from QueryDirectivesSuite.scala (test 'query with directive (3)', lines 116-148). Demonstrates that Result.Warning (emitted via Elab.warning during elaboration) produces a response containing BOTH the errors array and the data field — the distinguishing behaviour of Warning vs Failure.

minimalExamples.title: A compile failure becomes an errors-only response
minimalExamples.code:
val query = """ query { root { hidden } } """
val expected = json"""
  { "errors" : [ { "message" : "No field 'hidden' for type Root" } ] }
"""
TestCirceMapping.compileAndRun(query)  // IO[Json] == expected (no "data" key)
minimalExamples.explanation: Verbatim from CirceSuite.scala (lines 295-317). Compilation produced a Result.Failure, so mkResponse emits only the errors array with no data field. Contrast with the Warning example which keeps data.

minimalExamples.title: Lifting Result into an effect with ResultT
minimalExamples.explanation: ResultT threads Result through an effect F; flatMap preserves Warning/Failure/InternalError accumulation. This is the pattern used throughout queryinterpreter.scala and mapping.scala (e.g. ResultT(mapping.combineAndRun(queries))). Constructors mirror the Result companion.

gotchas: InternalError is NOT a GraphQL error. mkResponse(result: Result[Json]) calls M.raiseError(err) for InternalError, so it propagates as an effect-level failure (e.g. an IO error) rather than appearing in the errors array. Use Result.failure / Problem for client-facing errors and Result.internalError only for genuine bugs/unexpected conditions.

Failure has no value, Warning does. The whole point of Warning is to keep partial data while still reporting problems — it serialises to a response with BOTH data and errors. Choosing failure vs warning during elaboration changes whether the client gets any data (see the explicit comment in QueryDirectivesSuite: 'We could make this fail the whole query by yielding Elab.failure here').

Problem equality ignores extensions. eqProblem is Eq.by(p => (p.message, p.locations, p.path)) — two Problems with different extensions compare equal. Tests relying on extensions must compare the encoded JSON (asJson), not the Problem values.

Empty locations/path/extensions vanish from the JSON. The ProblemEncoder omits any empty field, so Problem("foo") encodes to just {"message":"foo"}. Don't assert on the presence of those keys when they're empty.

mkResponse(data=None, errors=empty) injects a synthetic error. If both data is absent and the error chain is empty it emits {"errors":[{"message":"Invalid query"}]} — an empty Result should never reach this path in normal flow, but a custom interpreter that returns no data and no problems will get this catch-all message.

combine / Semigroup downgrades Failure to Warning when the other side has a value. Result.combine of a Failure with a Success yields a Warning (problems + the success value), not a Failure. This is intentional Ior-like accumulation but can surprise callers expecting failure to dominate. InternalError, however, always dominates / short-circuits.

flatMap problem-merge order matters. In flatMap of a Warning whose continuation is a Warning, problems are concatenated as `problems ++ fps` (outer first). When relying on ordered error reporting, be aware combinators preserve a specific accumulation order (and Applicative ap orders them ff-then-fa).

Parallel/Applicative accumulate; Monad short-circuits. parMapN (via grackleParallelForResult) and the Applicative ap collect problems from all operands, but flatMap/for-comprehensions short-circuit on the first Failure/InternalError. Use parMapN / mapN / traverse when you want all errors reported at once (this is how the compiler reports multiple validation errors).

ValidationFailure is a different axis from Problem. ValidationFailure (with Severity Error/Warning/Info, ANSI colouring, ValidationException) is used at Schema/Mapping construction & validation time, not for per-request GraphQL errors. Don't confuse Result.Warning (runtime, a Problem) with Severity.Warning (a validation diagnostic).

fromOption/fromEither have DummyImplicit-disambiguated String overloads. The Problem and String variants of fromOption/fromEither (and Option#toResult) are distinguished by an implicit DummyImplicit because they'd otherwise erase to the same signature — passing the wrong by-name type can pick the unexpected overload.

Result.warning(String, value) wraps the string in a Problem with no path/locations. Warnings/failures created from bare strings have empty locations and path; positional info must be attached explicitly (e.g. via Problem(msg, locations, path)) or earlier in the pipeline, otherwise the errors array entry is message-only.
